title: Client recovery pathways and SLA choice notice
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a customer-facing draft bundle: short statuspage copy for immediate posting, an explanatory post-incident summary written in plain language, and a set of clear, actionable recovery choices customers can opt into (replay, selective replay, data export, or SLA credit). The intent is to give affected clients control over how they want Redwood to remediate their workloads and to reduce back-and-forth support friction.

Short status page update (for status.redwood.com):
Title: Partial inference impact in US-east region — recovery choices available
Status: Monitoring
Summary: On 2030-04-11 21:38 UTC we experienced routing and cache-coherence failures affecting a subset of inference requests in the US-east region. Most requests succeeded after automated retries; a minority of requests returned stale or truncated responses. The platform is stable and serving normally for the majority of traffic. We are offering replay and remediation options to impacted tenants.
What we did: Immediate routing rule rollback, cache rehydration, and increased dedicated-pool capacity to prevent reoccurrence.
Next steps: Customers who observe incorrect outputs can choose a replay or request a verification package (details below). A formal customer-facing post-incident summary is available here [link to confluence].

Long-form customer summary (plain-language postmortem):
Incident window: 2030-04-11 21:38 UTC — 2030-04-12 03:12 UTC (intermittent effects; mitigations in place by 22:05 UTC)
Impact: ~0.6% of total hosted API requests in US-east returned incomplete generation outputs or stale prefixed completions (customers that rely on strict deterministic outputs or downstream tokenization/validation were most affected). No data exfiltration; request metadata and payloads remained within normal retention and access controls.
Root cause (summary): A recent routing optimization rule intended to reduce cross-pool latencies introduced a subtle ordering regression with our KV-prefix cache invalidation logic. Under bursty traffic the cache invalidation did not always reach the target worker before the next request was served, which allowed stale KV cache state to be used for a small number of requests. This was compounded by a fallback configuration that re-routed these requests to a model variant that had a shorter context-checkpoint, producing truncated outputs for some request shapes.
What we fixed: We rolled back the routing change, added an explicit cache invalidation handshake (RPC ack) between the control plane and workers, and disabled the automatic fallthrough to the truncated-context variant. We also added a short, high-priority revalidation window in the dispatcher to catch stale-cache edge cases during burst conditions.
Verification: We ran targeted replays of representative customer traffic, synthetic stress tests, and a 2-hour shadow run while validating output shape and token alignment. No further stale outputs were observed during those runs.

Customer remediation options (choose one):
1) Opt-in full replay (recommended for high-integrity workloads): Redwood will replay impacted requests on the corrected routing/cache codepath within a read-only sandbox. Replay will be rate-limited to avoid downstream throttling; results delivered as a zip of response pairs (original response + replayed response) along with a verification checksum report. Timeline: typical completion in 24–72 hours depending on volume.
2) Selective replay by trace IDs / time window: Provide a list of request IDs, conversation IDs, or a time range and we will only replay those. Useful when customers can scope affected traffic narrowly.
3) Export-only verification package: If you prefer to self-verify, we will produce a package that contains request payloads (redacted per your retention policy), timestamps, routing metadata, and checksums. No replay performed.
4) SLA credit and opt-out of replay: For customers who prefer credit over remediation, we offer an SLA adjustment for the affected billing window. This option includes a short validation report (summary level) but not a replay.
5) Dedicated account remediation support: For enterprise customers with complex pipelines (webhooks, async processors, or downstream dedupe logic) we offer a hands-on remediation engagement with a Solutions Engineer to coordinate re-ingestion or targeted re-runs.

How to choose and next steps:
- If you need integrity for specific user-visible outputs (in chat transcripts, legal text, or billing-critical tokens), choose full replay or selective replay.
- If you have very high request volume and only a sample appears affected, use selective replay to scope verification cost.
- To elect SLA credit, reply to this notice with your account ID and the phrase "SLA CREDIT REQUEST" and we will return a proposed credit within 5 business days.
To request an action: open a support ticket with subject line "2030-04-11 US-east replay request: <your-account-id>" and include which option above you select, any trace IDs or time ranges (ISO8601), and your preferred contact for coordination. We will acknowledge within 2 business hours and provide an ETA.

Operational details customers may ask about:
- Are logs safe? Yes — all system logs and request payloads were retained in our secure logging cluster. We are not sharing any extra internal telemetry beyond what you request.
- Will replay change billing? Replayed generation units will be provided at no charge for the portion that is a direct remediation of the incident. Replays for new experiments or additional probes will be billed normally.
- Will replay affect downstream systems? We will perform replays in a sandboxed execution path and deliver responses; any re-ingestion into your downstream systems is your choice. For account remediation engagements, the Solutions team can assist with safe replay-to-production patterns.

Internal notes for CS agents (do not send verbatim):
- Prioritize accounts with deterministic downstream validation (payment processors, e-signature systems, compliance logs).
- Use template A for enterprise customers (detailed SLA language) and template B for low-volume self-serve customers.
- If customer selects replay, tag JIRA-INC-20330 and assign to remediation queue (remediation-engineering@redwood.com). Expected turnaround: 24–72 hours depending on token volume.
- For SLA credit requests, use internal billing code SLA2030-APR and route to finance-ops for approval.

Draft email subject suggestions (short and long):
Short: Redwood incident 2030-04-11 — replay and SLA choices
Long: Action required: Choose replay or SLA credit for 2030-04-11 US-east inference integrity event

Sample concise email body for customers (one-paragraph):
On 2030-04-11 we observed intermittent responses affected by a routing and cache ordering regression in US-east. The platform is now stable; you can request an opt-in replay, a verification package, or an SLA credit. Please reply with your account ID and preferred remediation option and we will acknowledge within 2 business hours.

Template attachments to include in support replies:
- Short checklist: What we need from you (account ID, time range, sample trace IDs).
- Privacy note: what data we will include in replays and what we redact.
- Expected timeline table for replay sizes (S, M, L).

Open questions / decisions needed from leadership:
- Approve the no-charge replay policy for remediation (recommended).
- Confirm SLA credit formula for customers who opt out of replay (percent of affected window).
- Decide whether to proactively run replays for accounts with automated compliance checks (recommended: run only with customer opt-in).

End of draft.
